newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down on currency, weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down on currency, weak demand.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended lower on technical adjustment following a surge of the local currency's value, traders said.

Business was also weak because institutional consumers in the United States and Europe had met most of their import requirements for the first quarter and were not ready for new commitments, said traders.
"The market's been quite the whole day," said a trader. "I think we need further (price) adjustments to see even some short-covering."

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted February RSS1 buyer at 305 cents ($1.25) a kg, down 1.50 cents from Friday. February SMR20 ended two cents lower at 302 cents a kg.
Trading houses were offering the SMR 20 at 305 cents a kg, the SMR CV at 367, SMR L at 349, SMR 10 at 305 and drum latex FOB at 238.
The INRO five-day average was 238.96 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Jan 10 from 239.90 on Jan 9. The daily indicator was 237.41 against 238.24 previously.
